messages.subject: log-log-scale: ordinate’s auxiliary lines off
parts:
Dear ggplot2 folks,


using ggplot2 to plot data with log-log-scale(?) the auxiliary lines for
the ordinate axis(?) are put right in the middle between 10^{-1.4} and
10^{-1.45} and not as expected a little off.

On the abscissa the help lines seem to be placed “logarithmicly”(?).
This only started to appear at a certain “zoom”/detail level.

In that a bug or a feature?

The plot is attached and I use the following commands.

> # read in z, if data is wanted, I can provide it
> z = 1 - cumsum(z/1e6)
> n = 1L:(1e6L + 2L)
> qplot(n[seq.int(1e5L,length(n),100L)], z[seq.int(1e5L,length(z),100L)]) + scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10()


Thanks,

Paul

On this scale, a little off is a very very little:

x <- -c(1.4, 1.45)
10 ^ mean(x)
mean(10 ^ x)
